# Install and operate codex-autoupdate

Act as the installer. Perform the installation and verify it; do not ask the
user to choose a Go binary directory or manually register launchd.

This software is for macOS. It requires Go and a logged-in administrator
account. It manages ChatGPT Desktop and Claude Desktop from one per-user
LaunchAgent, `com.tylergannon.codex-autoupdate`, and never uses `sudo`. Both
harnesses are enabled by default; missing applications are skipped.

## Install or upgrade

Download the installer, verify its published content hash, inspect it, and run
it:

```sh
installer=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tylergannon/codex-autoupdate/main/install.sh -o "$installer"
printf '%s  %s\n' d0fe9aa28d576d9f24520a2de6d1fc8762ea56c13a2e4c780dd7762b6fb2a44d "$installer" | shasum -a 256 -c -
sed -n '1,220p' "$installer"
bash "$installer"
```

The installer always selects the latest tagged release with:

```sh
go install github.com/tylergannon/codex-autoupdate/cmd/codex-autoupdate@latest
```

It upgrades an existing installation in place and refreshes its LaunchAgent.
Pass global flags through the installer to persist configuration:

```sh
bash "$installer" --idle-window 10m --poll-interval 30m
bash "$installer" --harness claude
bash "$installer" --chatgpt-app-path /absolute/path/ChatGPT.app \
  --claude-app-path /absolute/path/Claude.app
```

`--harness` accepts `chatgpt` or `claude` and may be repeated or comma-separated.
Without it, both are enabled. `--app-path` remains an alias for
`--chatgpt-app-path`.

## Verify and operate

```sh
binary="$HOME/Library/Application Support/codex-autoupdate/codex-autoupdate"
"$binary" --version
"$binary" status
"$binary" check --json
```

`check` is read-only and reports each selected harness independently. Logs are
under `~/Library/Logs/codex-autoupdate/`.

One-shot commands:

```sh
"$binary" run --once
"$binary" run --once --harness chatgpt
"$binary" update
"$binary" update --force
"$binary" update --force --harness claude
```

`update --force` bypasses only the requirement that the official release be
newer. It reinstalls an equal latest version, refuses an older release, waits
for activity to become idle, and retains every verification and rollback
safeguard. Force mode is never persisted in the LaunchAgent.

The installed watcher normally owns the shared coordinator lock. A one-shot
command writes a per-cache takeover request and wakes the watcher; the watcher
yields only after its current coordinator step is safe. The one-shot then uses
the same lock and cache. Launchd resumes the watcher after the request is
removed. A second one-shot command never signals the first one-shot and instead
exits with a contention error. Do not work around lock contention with a second
`--cache-dir`.

Uninstall with:

```sh
"$binary" uninstall
```

Uninstall removes the LaunchAgent plist and canonical binary. Logs, downloads,
and quarantine markers remain for diagnosis.

## Activity and replacement behavior

The watcher discovers ChatGPT from OpenAI's stable Sparkle appcast and Claude
from Anthropic's desktop Squirrel update API. Each harness stages a complete
application bundle and owns an independent uninterrupted idle window.

Active means Codex, Claude Code, or Claude Cowork work is currently executing.
Open UI windows, ordinary chat use, dormant sessions, configured schedules, and
future scheduled work do not count. Unreadable activity state fails closed for
that harness and polling cycle. Claude detection covers Desktop session
workers, standalone Claude Code processes, and Claude task processes that still
hold task output streams.

Immediately before replacement, the updater repeats the activity and installed
version checks. It then:

1. verifies the advertised version, pinned bundle identifier and signing team,
   strict code signature, Gatekeeper acceptance, and host architecture;
2. asks the exact application to quit normally;
3. if quit is refused, re-resolves the exact main PID and sends `SIGTERM`;
4. confirms process absence, atomically replaces the bundle, relaunches it, and
   verifies the signed expected version became ready.

It never sends `SIGKILL`. Replacements are serialized in `chatgpt`, then
`claude` order. A busy, missing, or failed harness does not block the other.

## Recovery

If a replacement does not become ready, the prior application is restored and
relaunched. Rollback uses the same graceful-quit and exact-main-PID `SIGTERM`
path and will not move a running failed replacement. The failed version is
quarantined separately under:

```text
~/Library/Caches/codex-autoupdate/chatgpt/failed-version-VERSION.json
~/Library/Caches/codex-autoupdate/claude/failed-version-VERSION.json
```

A newer version remains eligible. Remove a marker only when deliberately
retrying that same version. Staging, residue, rollback, and quarantine state is
partitioned by harness. If the updater or machine stops after moving the prior
bundle but before activating its replacement, the next watcher start verifies
the single retained rollback bundle, restores it to the canonical path, and
relaunches it. Multiple possible rollback bundles fail closed for manual
inspection.

Repository proof and operator notes are under
`ephemeral/projects/codex-autoupdate/`.
